recipe_name: Fermented Cherry Semolina Cake with Cherry Pit Elixir
visual_description: A single, elegantly cut rectangular slice of golden-hued semolina cake rests on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate. The cake's surface is subtly textured, hinting at the semolina, with small, deep red pieces of fermented cherry visible within its crumb. Adjacent to the cake, a small, organic pool of glistening, amber-toned cherry pit elixir reflects the soft natural light. A few whole, plump, deep ruby-red fermented cherries are artfully placed near the cake, their slightly wrinkled skins offering a natural, rustic texture. A single, vibrant green mint sprig is gently laid beside the cake, providing a fresh contrast. The composition is clean and unforced, with ample white space on the plate. The plate sits on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by a folded undyed linen napkin in natural beige. The background is minimalist, with a hint of soft green foliage from a nearby plant, enhancing the eco-conscious aesthetic. The lighting is soft and natural, emphasizing the pure beauty and natural colors of each ingredient.

ingredients.name: fresh mint sprigs or small edible flowers

instructions: Wash cherries. Pit cherries. Reserve pits for elixir.
Place pitted cherries in a clean jar. Dissolve 5g salt in 250ml filtered water. Pour brine over cherries, ensuring they are fully submerged.
Seal jar loosely. Ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-5 days. Burp daily. Refrigerate once desired tanginess is achieved.

Rinse cherry pits. Place pits in a small saucepan with 200ml water. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat. Simmer gently for 15 minutes. Strain out pits. Discard pits. Return liquid to saucepan. Stir in 20g maple syrup. Simmer until slightly reduced and syrupy, about 5-7 minutes. Cool completely.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Lightly grease and flour a 20cm x 10cm loaf pan or a small 15cm round cake pan.
In a large bowl, whisk together semolina flour, all-purpose flour, baking powder, baking soda, and 2g salt.
In a separate bowl, whisk together plant-based milk, 100g maple syrup, neutral oil, and vanilla extract.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Gently fold in 50g of roughly chopped fermented cherries.
Pour batter into prepared pan. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Remove cake from oven. Let cool in pan for 10 minutes. Invert onto a wire rack to cool completely.
Slice cooled cake into 4 equal rectangular portions. Place one slice on each serving plate.
Drizzle generously with cherry pit elixir. Arrange a few whole fermented cherries next to the cake. Garnish with a fresh mint sprig or edible flower.

recipe_name: Cherry & Ricotta Ravioli with Brown Butter Sage Sauce
visual_description: A single portion of Cherry & Ricotta Ravioli is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Four to five plump, golden-yellow ravioli are arranged naturally, slightly overlapping, at the center of the plate. The pasta surface is smooth, with subtle hints of the dark red cherry filling visible beneath. A glossy, rich brown butter sauce liberally coats each raviolo, pooling slightly around them. Crisp, deep green sage leaves are scattered artfully over the dish, providing a textural contrast. A generous sprinkle of finely grated Parmesan cheese adds a light, powdery finish. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, a grey cotton napkin folded neatly beside the plate, and standard Italian-style flatware. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its warmth and rustic elegance. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra freshly grated Pecorino Romano or Parmesan cheese on the side.
Offer crusty Italian bread to sop up the delicious brown butter sauce.

ingredients.name: Fresh cherries, pitted and finely diced

instructions: On a clean surface, combine semolina and '00' flour. Make a well in the center. Crack eggs into the well. Add a pinch of salt.
Gradually incorporate flour into eggs using a fork, then hands. Knead dough for 10-15 minutes until smooth and elastic. Add water sparingly if dough is too dry.
Wrap dough in plastic film. Let rest at room temperature for 30 minutes.
In a bowl, combine ricotta, finely diced cherries, grated Parmesan, lemon zest, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Divide pasta dough into four portions. Roll one portion thinly using a pasta machine or rolling pin. Aim for a thickness of about 1 mm.
Place small spoonfuls of filling (about 1 teaspoon) onto half of the pasta sheet, spaced 3 cm apart.
Moisten edges around filling with water. Fold the other half of the pasta sheet over the filling. Press down gently to seal, removing air pockets.
Cut individual ravioli using a fluted pastry wheel or knife. Repeat with remaining dough and filling.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Carefully add ravioli. Cook for 3-4 minutes, or until they float and are tender. Do not overcrowd the pot.
While ravioli cooks, melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook until butter turns golden brown and smells nutty (beurre noisette). Add sage leaves. Cook until crispy.
Using a slotted spoon, transfer cooked ravioli directly into the brown butter sage sauce. Gently toss to coat.
Serve immediately. Garnish with additional grated Parmesan and fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For best results, use fresh, firm cherries.
The pasta dough should be firm but pliable. Adjust flour or water as needed.
Do not overfill the ravioli to prevent bursting during cooking.

visual_description: A single elegant slice of Blueberry Lemon Ricotta Cake is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The cake slice is moist and tender, revealing a scattering of whole, plump blueberries within its pale, creamy yellow crumb. A few additional whole blueberries are artfully placed around the base of the slice. The cake has a delicate golden-brown crust on top, adorned with a few slightly burst, caramelized blueberries. A fine dusting of lemon zest provides a vibrant visual and aromatic counterpoint. The setting is a modern bistro style with a simple wooden table surface. A crisp white cotton napkin is neatly folded beside the plate. In the background, a portion of the whole cake rests on a minimalist cake stand, hinting at its full, inviting form. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the cake's inviting texture and fresh colors.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and flour a 20 cm round cake pan.
In a large bowl, whisk together ricotta cheese, eggs, olive oil, lemon zest, lemon juice, and vanilla extract until smooth.
In a separate bowl, combine flour, baking powder, and salt.
Gradually add dry ingredients to wet ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Gently fold in 200 g of blueberries into the batter.
Pour batter into prepared cake pan. Scatter remaining 100 g blueberries on top.
Bake for 40-45 minutes, or until a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Cool cake in pan for 10 minutes. Invert onto a wire rack to cool completely.
notes: Use very ripe, sweet blueberries to maximize natural sweetness since no sugar is added.
The cake's sweetness level relies entirely on the natural sugars in the blueberries. For those accustomed to traditional sugary cakes, this will be a subtly sweet, more dessert-like bread.

recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Potato Gratin
visual_description: A golden-brown square of creamy potato gratin, its bubbly Gruyère crust glistening, forms the inviting base on a pristine white porcelain plate. Thick-cut, pan-seared chicken medallions, displaying a beautiful golden crust and tender interior, are artfully placed on top of the gratin, slightly overlapping. The dish showcases rich golden-browns, creamy whites, and vibrant green flecks from fresh parsley. Textures include the crispy chicken skin, creamy potato layers, and melted cheese. A delicate sprinkle of chopped fresh parsley garnishes the entire dish. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded grey cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the dish as the centerpiece in a clean, modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Lightly butter a 20x20 cm baking dish.
Peel potatoes. Slice thinly, about 2-3 mm thick, using a mandoline or sharp knife.
In a medium saucepan, combine cream, minced garlic, and thyme sprigs. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Remove from heat. Season with salt and pepper.
Arrange one-third of the sliced potatoes in a single layer in the prepared baking dish. Season lightly with salt and pepper.
Pour one-third of the cream mixture over the potatoes. Sprinkle with one-third of the grated Gruyère.
Repeat layering with remaining potatoes, cream, and cheese. Ensure top layer of potatoes is covered with cream and cheese.
Bake for 50-60 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and top is golden and bubbly. If browning too quickly, cover with foil.
While gratin bakes, pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil and butter in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 5-7 minutes per side, until deep golden brown. Transfer skillet to oven for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Let rest 5 minutes.
Slice chicken breasts into thick-cut medallions.
Remove gratin from oven. Let rest 5 minutes.
To serve, cut gratin into four portions. Place one portion on each plate. Arrange chicken medallions on top. Garnish with fresh parsley or chives.

recipe_name: Blueberry Mousse with Almond Oat Crisp
visual_description: A single portion of light purple blueberry mousse sits elegantly in a clear, stemmed dessert glass on a clean white porcelain plate. The mousse, with its airy texture, fills the glass to about two-thirds, showing its delicate, pale lavender hue. A scattering of whole, plump, fresh blueberries, deep indigo in color, rests on top, some gently nestled into the mousse. Beside the glass, a small pile of golden-brown almond oat crisp pieces provides a textural contrast, their irregular shapes adding a rustic yet refined touch. The plate has ample negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table surface and a white cotton napkin folded beside the plate. Natural, soft light illuminates the scene, highlighting the mousse's sheen and the blueberries' natural bloom.
instructions: Bloom gelatin in cold water. Set aside.
Blend 200g blueberries until smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve to remove skins. Set aside. Keep 50g blueberries for garnish.
Whisk egg yolks in a heatproof bowl. Heat milk in a saucepan until simmering. Gradually whisk hot milk into egg yolks.
Return mixture to saucepan. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until thickened to coat the back of a spoon. Do not boil.
Remove from heat. Stir in bloomed gelatin until dissolved. Stir in blueberry puree and lemon zest.
Pour mixture into a clean bowl. Place bowl over an ice bath. Stir occasionally until mixture cools and thickens slightly, about 15-20 minutes.
In a separate chilled bowl, whip heavy cream to soft peaks.
Gently fold whipped cream into the cooled blueberry base in two additions. Mix until just combined.
Pour mousse into four individual serving glasses or molds. Chill in refrigerator for at least 4 hours, or until set.
Preheat oven to 160°C. Combine oats, almond flour, melted butter, and salt in a bowl. Mix until crumbly.
Spread mixture thinly on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Bake for 10-15 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp. Let cool completely. Break into small pieces.
Spoon or pipe mousse into serving dishes. Garnish with remaining fresh blueberries and crumbled almond oat crisp.
notes: This recipe relies on the natural sweetness of ripe blueberries. No additional sugar is used.
